reviewMethod: Independent visual inspection of all eight original paper pages and scheme pages 33–76, including every optional question, published allocation, attempt floor, original diagram and alternative method. All 60 question and 60 complete solution presentations inspected.
sourceNotes: Attempt five questions from Section A and one from Section B is whole-examination selection. Retain all tasks in all eleven questions, including all four Section B options. Do not create duplicate examination bundles.
A marble follows one path: this describes the random experiment, not a choice of practice task. Both other paths to H are required in Q7(b)(i). All events and subparts remain carded.

Q10(b)(i) and (ii) ask the student to construct an example of a symmetry with a specified order and describe it geometrically. No finite pool of printed answers is offered. The scheme lists the number of possible correct examples but these are alternative valid answers, not selectable printed routes. Later tasks retain the dependency on the chosen x and y.
All roots, angles, vectors, inverses and proofs requested together remain required. Published alternative solution methods stay inside the relevant card.
Mathematical errors or omissions: −3. Numerical slips: −1. Misreadings: −1 provided the task is not oversimplified.
A correct relevant step earns its attempt mark; deductions cannot reduce it below that floor. No mark strictly between zero and the attempt mark.
Worthless work: zero. Hit or miss: full marks or zero.
Best of two or more attempts accepted unless indicated otherwise; same error in same section penalised once.
Particular cases, unrequested verifications/diagrams, and serious blunders/omissions/misreadings earn attempt marks at most.
Detailed task-specific exceptions and caps must remain beside all official worked alternatives.
The independent paper/scheme sweep identifies 60 printed tasks, with 50 offered marks in each of eleven questions. Section A is Q1–Q7; Section B is Q8–Q11.

Q2(c)(i) requires both vector expressions, Q10(b)(i)/(ii) each require a permutation and its geometrical description, and Q11(b)(ii) requires a linked transformation proof. Their separately allocated components remain visible within each printed task.
Setup, algebra, differentiation and completion allocations are steps of one response, not additional questions.

Historical vectors and transformations are placed with coordinate geometry, group operations with algebra, and the ellipse with coordinate geometry of the circle. These are existing canonical navigation topics, not a claim that these historical optional topics belong to the current syllabus. No historical question is hidden.
Q3(a) retains the explicit exception to the usual best-of-attempts rule.
Q5(c)(ii), Q8(b)(ii) and Q8(c)(ii) retain their task-specific restrictions from earlier work.
Q8(a) omitting the integration constant is a one-mark slip, as this paper specifies.
Q9(c)(i), Q10(b)(v) and Q11(b)(ii) retain original printing errors with explanatory source notes; no invented marks or criteria.

cards.questionText: Given A′ = f(A) and B′ = f(B), show that ∠AOB ≠ ∠A′OB′.

cards.questionText: Let S = {e, x, y, x ∘ y, y ∘ x, x ∘ x}, where e is the identity. Show that S is not closed under composition.

cards.questionText: Show that |f(P)f(Q)|/|PQ| = √[(2 cos θ + 5 sin θ)² + (3 cos θ + 4 sin θ)²].
cards.stem: P(x₁, y₁) and Q(x₂, y₂) satisfy x₁ < x₂. The slope of PQ is tan θ and its length is d. The transformation f is x′ = 2x + 5y + 6, y′ = 3x + 4y + 1.

cards.questionText: Deduce that the ratio of lengths on parallel lines is invariant under f.
cards.stem: P(x₁, y₁) and Q(x₂, y₂) satisfy x₁ < x₂. The slope of PQ is tan θ and its length is d. The transformation f is x′ = 2x + 5y + 6, y′ = 3x + 4y + 1. The preceding part establishes |f(P)f(Q)|/|PQ| = √[(2 cos θ + 5 sin θ)² + (3 cos θ + 4 sin θ)²].
